scope: Theorem 2.2 (The geometric deformation) of the manuscript “The spacetime Penrose inequality and enclosing area” (preprints/The-spacetime-Penrose-inequality-and-enclosing-area-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 260 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 9bb0c350914915db), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 8. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a prepared exterior and 0 < ϵ < 1. For all sufficiently large integers N there is a connected enclosing-set exterior XN , complete with its compact frontier ΣN included, in a smooth Riemannian ambient metric ˜︁ gN . It has one Euclidean coordinate end with compact complement, and R˜︁ gN ≥ 0, R˜︁ gN ∈ L1 (XN ), ˜︁ gN − δ = O2(r2−n ), R˜︁ gN = O(r−n−β′ ) for some β′ > 0, E(˜︁ gN ) ≤ E0 + PN (e−Nϵ + e−Nϵ/2 ), Hn−1 ˜︁ gN (ΣN ) ≥ e−(n−1)ϵ A0. (2.2) Here PN is a polynomial in N, with coefficients depending on the fixed datum and ϵ. The metric is smooth through the frontier. The whole frontier is outer minimizing and locally perimeter minimizing as the boundary of its filled side. It is smooth embedded minimal away from a compact singular set of Hausdorff dimension at most n − 8; for 3 ≤ n ≤ 7 the singular set is empty. Its area counts every component.
